architecture.scope: Windows desktop diagnostics shell with a portable native C policy/evidence core and optional Swift backend.
architecture.runtime_boundary: Windows host application; portable core remains separately testable.
architecture.composition_rule: Keep device discovery, evidence normalization, guidance and reporting as bounded modules behind explicit read-only interfaces.

components.responsibility: Normalize observations and preserve unknown versus failed states.
Explain evidence quality and safe next steps.
Optional backend boundary; not required by the portable C core.

dependencies.relationship: selected native policy rules ported into C17; not Python runtime embedding

preserved_boundaries: All hardware observation is read-only by default.
Unknown, unavailable, incomplete and failed evidence remain distinct.
Windows-specific UI and device access remain host-targeted.
forbidden_composition: No silent device or driver mutation.
No cloud upload of diagnostic reports by default.
No implicit privilege transfer from the UI to helper processes.
gaps: Run Windows-host build and device-enumeration tests on supported Windows versions.
Prove packaging, signing and optional backend interoperability separately.
